data.title: Biodexa Pharmaceuticals enters warrant exercise transaction for $2.3M gross proceeds; shares rise
data.description:
• Biodexa Pharmaceuticals (BDRX) has entered into a warrant exercise agreement to exercise certain outstanding warrants to purchase an aggregate of 2.20M American depositary shares of the company at an exercise price of $1.05 for gross cash proceeds of ~$2.3M.
  • The exercising holder will receive new unregistered warrants to purchase an aggregate of up to 4.41M ADSs.
  • The new warrants will have an exercise price of $1.05, will be immediately exercisable upon issuance, and will have a term of exercise of five years.
  • The closing of the warrant inducement transaction is expected to occur on or about September 15, 2026.
  • BDRX shares up 18% premarket.

data.title: Amerant Bancorp prices $50M notes offering
data.description:
• Amerant Bancorp (AMTB) priced an offering of $50M senior notes due 2031, with the notes carrying a 7% annual interest rate.
  • The unsecured, unsubordinated notes will mature on Sept. 17, 2031, with interest payable semiannually on March 17 and Sept. 17 beginning in March 2027.
  • The offering is expected to close Sept. 17, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions. The company intends to use the net proceeds from this offering for general corporate purposes.

data.title: RB Global increases share repurchase program from $500M to $1B
data.description:
• RB Global (RBA) announced that Toronto Stock Exchange has approved an amendment to its current normal course issuer bid to increase the maximum number of common shares that may be repurchased to be the lesser of 14.22M shares, representing ~10% of the total public float, and that number of shares worth an aggregate of US$1B.
  • No other terms of the NCIB have been amended.
  • The NCIB, launched on March 18, 2026, originally allowed repurchase up to the lesser of 10M shares.
  • As of September 11, 2026, RBA has repurchased 5.36M shares at an average price of ~US$93.22 per share.
  • The NCIB will terminate on March 17, 2027.

data.title: AI search firm Profound's latest funding round values it at $1.8B
data.description:
New York City–based AI marketing startup Profound has raised $180M in a Series D financing that values it at $1.8B. The round was co-led by Sequoia Capital and Kleiner Perkins and takes the company’s cumulative funding to more than $335M.

Profound's valuation rise has been exceptionally fast. It raised a $20M Series A in 2025 led by Kleiner Perkins, followed by a $35M Series B led by Sequoia Capital in August 2025. At that time, it said its platform was being used daily by roughly 2,000 marketers across more than 500 organizations, including customers such as Ramp, U.S. Bank, Indeed, MongoDB, DocuSign, and Chime.

The company operates in the emerging field often called answer-engine optimization, or AEO. Its initial product tracked how often AI models named a brand in response to relevant prompts, the language used to describe it, and the competitive brands that appeared alongside it. Profound has expanded this into a broader platform that helps marketing teams analyze AI visibility, identify content gaps, create material intended to improve discoverability, and use AI agents to support marketing campaigns.

Looking back, Profound was created by CEO James Cadwallader and CTO Dylan Babbs to address a major shift in online discovery as people increasingly ask conversational AI systems, such as ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Claude, Perplexity, Grok, and Microsoft Copilot, for recommendations and information rather than relying solely on conventional Google search results. For brands, that increases the need to understand AI assistants instead of optimizing to rank among search results. Brands also have to ensure that they are described accurately.

Profound competes at least partially against companies like HubSpot (HUBS), Adobe (ADBE), and Similarweb (SMWB).

data.title: General Motors makes room for CarPlay and Android Auto in 2027 Silverado, Sierra
data.description:
After ditching phone mirroring to get drivers to use its native software, General Motors (GM) is giving new Chevy Silverado and GMC Sierra truck owners a way to integrate Apple’s CarPlay (AAPL) and Google’s Android Auto (GOOG) (GOOGL) into the infotainment system without giving up screen space for its own software.

General Motors (GM) dropped Apple CarPlay (AAPL) and Google’s Android Auto (GOOG) (GOOGL) from its EVs three years ago in an effort to take full control of its in-car software and collect driver data that apps like CarPlay and Android Auto do not provide to the car manufacturer. It also provides car manufacturers like GM (GM) an additional revenue stream through app subscriptions with their own vehicle software. 

But starting with the newest models of the Silverado and Sierra, GM (GM) is giving owners a new way to connect their phones to the vehicle’s native software.

By using picture-in-picture phone mirroring, GM (GM) engineers have found a way to give drivers the option to use phone projection while at the same time keeping GM’s native software front and center. Now, CarPlay and Android Auto occupy a contextual card rather than use an entire screen.

“I think we’re landing in a spot where we don’t have a customer who has to decide, 'Oh, I’m going to use projection or I want to use the native system.' That’s our sweet spot,” said GM’s group product manager for Google built-in projection, Colin McCormick, to The Verge.

data.title: Legend Biotech appoints Ingrid Zhang as CEO
data.description:
• Legend Biotech (LEGN) on Tuesday appointed Ingrid Zhang as Chief Executive Officer, effective September 15, 2026.
  • Zhang succeeds Alan Bash, who has served as interim CEO since July 2026.
  • Most recently, Zhang served as Chief Commercial Officer for Novartis International. During her tenure at Novartis, she also led the company's China business and innovative medicines organization. Earlier in her career, she held leadership positions at AstraZeneca, Pfizer, and McKinsey & Company.
  • Press release

data.title: Otis CEO Judy Marks to retire in 1H 2027
data.description:
• Otis Worldwide (OTIS) said Judy Marks will retire as chair, chief executive officer, and president upon the appointment of her successor, which is expected in the first half of 2027.
  • Otis board has launched a CEO search with Spencer Stuart advising the process. The search will consider both internal and external candidates, overseen by independent directors.
  • Marks will remain in her current role through July 31, 2027, or serve as senior adviser if a successor is named sooner.

data.title: NuRAN Wireless announces ATM offering
data.description:
• NuRAN Wireless (NUR) entered into an at the market offering agreement with H.C. Wainwright & Co on September 15, 2026.
  • NUR may offer and sell common shares having an aggregate offering price of up to US$50M.

data.title: Cognyte secures ~$10M contract with long-standing APAC national security customer
data.description:
• Cognyte Software (CGNT) on Tuesday said a long-standing national security customer in the Asia-Pacific (APAC) region has selected the company for a new contract valued at about $10M. 
  • The newly deployed capabilities are designed to help the customer scale secure intelligence operations, strengthen mission readiness and support increasingly demanding national security requirements.
  • Press release

data.title: RTX’s Pratt & Whitney advances F-35 engine upgrade toward production
data.description:
RTX’s (RTX) Pratt & Whitney has completed a design review of its planned F135 Engine Core Upgrade, advancing the program toward production for the F-35 fighter jet.

The risk reduction design review examined the upgrade’s detailed design, propulsion technologies, aircraft integration and testing preparations. It also assessed whether suppliers are prepared to support production and retrofits.

The upgrade is intended to provide the additional power and thermal-management capacity required for the F-35’s Block 4 modernization program. Block 4 calls for advanced sensors, weapons and other systems across all three variants of the aircraft.

For investors, the milestone reduces some of the technical and execution risk surrounding a program that could support long-term production and aftermarket revenue for RTX (RTX). The ability to retrofit existing aircraft also expands the potential market beyond newly built F-35s, although future revenue will depend on government funding, testing results and the timing of production contracts.

Pratt & Whitney Military Engines President Jill Albertelli said in a statement that the review demonstrated the design’s maturity and moved the company closer to delivering an upgrade based on the existing F135 architecture. U.S. Navy Capt. Mitch Grant, the F-35 propulsion program manager, said the project remains on schedule to support the aircraft’s modernization.

Risk-reduction work funded under a contract awarded in 2024 includes design development, aircraft integration, test preparation, engineering and supply-chain readiness. Pratt & Whitney said the upgrade is designed to be installed in newly produced aircraft or retrofitted at F135 maintenance depots.

The company has delivered more than 1,500 F135 engines to customers across 20 allied countries. Pratt & Whitney plans to retain substantial commonality with the current engine as it develops the upgrade, potentially limiting changes to the F-35’s existing production and maintenance network.
